title: Two-Letter Card Game
summary: Given a deck of cards as a string array, each card showing two lowercase letters, and a letter x, you score points by removing pairs of cards that both contain x in any position.
statement: Given a deck of cards as a string array, each card showing two lowercase letters, and a letter x, you score points by removing pairs of cards that both contain x in any position. Each valid pair earns one point. The game ends when no more pairs can be found. The task is to determine the maximum points achievable with optimal play, where two cards are considered compatible if they differ in exactly one position.
constraints: Two to 100,000 two-letter cards using letters a through j.
Both selected cards contain x and differ in exactly one position.
Remove cards in pairs to maximize the score.
hints: Cards with x only on the left and only on the right form separate complete multipartite matching groups; xx cards connect to both.
First maximize different-letter pairs within each side, then match xx cards to leftovers or free two cards by sacrificing a pair.
Compute each side’s min(total/2,total-largest) matching, consume natural leftovers, then exchange one pair for two center matches when useful.
The multipartite bound is attainable, and each remaining center either uses a leftover or requires breaking exactly one existing pair for two available cards.
editorial: The multipartite bound is attainable, and each remaining center either uses a leftover or requires breaking exactly one existing pair for two available cards.

tests.explanation: Pair ab-ac and aa-ba for two points.
Only one compatible pair can be removed.
